rationale: The 10-bead cut itself is sound: each bead is an independently reviewable deliverable with its own AC set (the 127 over-compression precedent is answered, and no bead is trivially mergeable — bead 9, the smallest, still carries AC-11's two-leg content+termsafe contract), the depth-4 chain (1→2→{4,5}→10) is genuinely forced (the row fixtures need option-1 value semantics AND honest state show; the docs describe beads 4/5's shipped behavior), beads 3/7/9 are correctly parallel-from-start, the AC-5 split across beads 1/2 is at the right grain (machinery vs value-semantics legs verified leg-by-leg), the Provenance table gives every AC including 4b and 10b exactly one home, and the work_chunks positional frontmatter matches every bead section's declared deps exactly (verified all 10). But three seam-precision defects need fixing before implementation subagents consume this plan per-bead: (1) bead 1's key_file_paths omit the six writer files its own step 3 edits, and key_file_paths is load-bearing — plan approve populates each bead's file_paths bd metadata from it (internal/approve/plan.go:602-623), which is both the bead's impl-context 'Key File Paths' surface and the declared-scope baseline for the complete-time bead-scope advisory (internal/complete/bead_scope.go:41); (2) the 'sanctioned entry' seam between beads 1 and 2 is unbuilt-by-anyone: bead 2's Depends-on says bead 1 supplies 'lock + guard + sanctioned entry' and the OQ-3 sanction boundary describes 'a non-exported guard-bypassing entry of the same locked write helper', but bead 1's steps place the backward guard in cmd/mindspec/repair.go only (step 4) and define a single WithPhaseWriteLock entry (step 2) — no step in either bead creates the guarded/sanctioned entry pair, the exact inter-bead-seam-leak class the spec-120 final review caught post-hoc; (3) the Decomposition Note's clean-seams claim ('beads share complete.go/next.go only where the dependency edges serialize them') is false as written — internal/phase/derive.go is shared by parallel beads 2 and 3 (no edge), internal/next/beads.go by parallel beads 8 and 9 (no edge, and chunk 8 lists beads.go with no corresponding step), cmd/mindspec/next.go by bead 7 (dep [1] only) vs beads 2/8, and internal/complete/complete.go by unserialized beads 5 and 6 — while same-file edges ARE granted for 8→2 and 6→1; the de facto region-level policy is defensible (bead 6's Depends-on states it well) but the note is the plan's in-document discharge of the validate WARN and must state the policy actually applied. All three are cheap document fixes that do not disturb the cut, the sequencing, or the OQ resolutions.

findings.title: The sanctioned lock-helper entry is attributed to bead 1 but appears in no bead's step list
findings.detail: Bead 2's 'Depends on' reads 'Bead 1 (lock + guard + sanctioned entry)' and the OQ-3 sanction-boundary paragraph describes release's sync routing through 'a non-exported guard-bypassing entry of the same locked write helper' — implying the helper enforces the backward guard for ordinary callers and exposes a bypass. But bead 1 step 2 defines exactly one entry (WithPhaseWriteLock) with no guard semantics, and step 4 places the backward comparator inside cmd/mindspec/repair.go as an operator-path guard. Neither bead's steps build the guarded/bypass entry pair. Under the serial per-bead subagent model, bead 1's implementer (reading only bead 1's section) ships without it and bead 2's implementer must improvise the architecture decision mid-bead — the inter-bead-seam gap class the plan's own review history (spec 120 final review) shows per-bead panels miss. One sentence pinning where the guard lives and which bead builds the internal entry closes it.

findings.title: Decomposition Note's clean-seams claim is factually wrong as written; edge policy applied inconsistently
findings.detail: The note claims 'beads share complete.go/next.go only where the dependency edges serialize them', but: internal/phase/derive.go is shared by beads 2 and 3, both parallel-eligible (2 dep [1], 3 dep []), no edge; internal/next/beads.go is shared by beads 8 and 9 (9 dep []), no edge — and bead 9's edit is inside QueryReady/QueryReadyForEpic (beads.go:38,54), plausibly the same functions bead 8's ordering work touches, while chunk 8 lists beads.go with no bead-8 step naming it; cmd/mindspec/next.go is edited by bead 7 (dep [1] only) with no edge to beads 2 or 8; internal/complete/complete.go is shared by unserialized beads 5 and 6. Meanwhile same-file overlap DID generate the 8→2 edge and (per its stated rationale) the 6→1 edge. The underlying region-level policy plus serial execution is sound — bead 6's Depends-on articulates it correctly — but the note is the plan's answer to the R=0.09 WARN and should state the real policy, not an only-where-serialized claim that four counterexamples in the plan's own frontmatter falsify.
